newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil winter not to be so harsh this year - Inmet.
newsitem.headline: Brazil winter not to be so harsh this year - Inmet.

text.p: Brazil's winter should not be as cold as last year's but that does not rule out the possibility of frosts in coffee areas, said a forecaster at Brazil's National Institute of Meteorology (Inmet).
"This should not be a harsh winter this year, temperatures should be more or less normal but there is still the risk of frosts in the coffee areas," said Francisco Assis.

Last year Inmet correctly predicted a colder winter than normal due to the "La Nina" weather phenomenon, with several cold air masses, particularly in July, causing temperatures to fall dangerously close to zero (C) on several occasions.

This year, minimum temperatures in Brazil's most southern coffee-growing region - north Parana - and its highest growing region - around Pocos de Caldas, south Minas Gerais state - should be around three or four degrees Celsius, Assis said.
The risk of frost would only really begin in the second half of June and run through to the end of July, he added.
Brazilian coffee farmers are hoping that next year's harvest will be the first to show a complete recovery from the impact of two frosts and a drought which hit the crop in 1994.
Any frost damage this year however would put an end to hopes to see a harvest of 30 million 60-kg bags or above.
